content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: delay 14:00-15:00 breaks by 45 min and offer IVR callbacks on both queues, at no extra cost, lifting service level to 89.9% for 13:45-15:45.","why":"The IMPS/NEFT payment hub fault (INC-20261112-1271) is resolved and payments calls are almost back to forecast (91 vs 85.8 at 13:30). Service level has been 100% since 13:00. Doing nothing would still give 85.7% overall, but general would sit at 79.9%, just under the 80% target. P1 costs nothing and brings general to 84.3% and payments to 94.1%. Abandons fall from 3.3% to 2.3%, and rest of day rises to 94.9%.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) also costs ₹0 but leaves general at 79.9%, below target, with 3.3% abandons.","P2 costs ₹324 for chat deflection, and it does slightly worse than P1 overall (89.6% vs 89.9%, general 83.5%, abandons 2.6%), so the spend isn't justified.","P3 gives the strongest result (93.6% overall, general 90.7%, abandons 1.7%, rest of day 96.4%) but costs ₹1,944 in overtime for a disruption that is already over.","P1 pushes agents' breaks back 45 minutes, and callbacks mean some customers get a call back rather than being answered straight away."],"watch":"Watch the general queue, which has the least headroom at 84.3%, along with the callback queue and the delayed breaks through 14:00-15:00. If payments volume climbs again or general drops toward 80%, move up to P3's overtime."}
